svg.title: The rubric and the marked page
svg.desc: A marking rubric with eleven criteria beside a marked report page with four margin brackets and a faculty style guide entry.

g.text: SCIENCE 2210 - LAB REPORT RUBRIC - ELEVEN CRITERIA, 100 MARKS
"we can conclude that it exists a relation"
One of the four is an error. The other three are current-English
preferences: allow, conclude, increase. A chemist in 1890 would
"Prefer short Anglo-Saxon verbs where they exist: use rather
than utilise, allow rather than permit, increase rather than
augment. This is a preference, not a rule."
WHO HAS READ THE STYLE GUIDE:
It is on a shelf in the main office. It is not on the unit site,
not in the handbook, and not referenced in any of the eleven
criteria. Three of nineteen staff surveyed knew it existed.
The rubric and the marked page
Eleven criteria, none about language, and four brackets in a margin.
Zero. And four marks came off for
One real error in four brackets,
and it is not the one that was
The guide itself says it is a
Three of nineteen staff knew it
